content.comment_body: Good morning, I've learned that the Initialization Flag M8 is set high for one cycle after startup, and then behaves as a standard flag in subsequent cycles. Is it possible to use M25 to M31 as regular flags too? I'm working with a [product_name], and do not require any backlight functions, so I'm hoping to repurpose those flags. Thank you for your assistance.

The only exception I am aware of involves the latest version of [product_name]: M27 is used for character set switching. Within the message text settings, you can configure whether M27 should serve this function. Access these settings under: File > Properties > Message text.

analysis.insight_summary: The user discussion highlights insufficient documentation regarding internal flags in [product_name] hardware. Users try to repurpose system flags for conventional uses, but most are reserved except for a single exception linked to a newer version and a specific feature. Limited configuration options and unclear boundaries between features cause users to feel uncertain about available resources.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect unrestricted use of memory flags, especially those not currently assigned to standard features in the product they are using.
